name: Dropshipping business
blurb: Sell online while a supplier ships each order straight to your customer, with no stock
title: Dropshipping Business: How to Start and What Can Go Wrong
description: How to start dropshipping: how it makes money, what you need, who it suits, the shipping and supplier risks, and how to test a product before spending on ads.
h1: How to start a dropshipping business
answer: Dropshipping means you run an online store, take the order and payment, and a supplier ships the product directly to the customer, so you never hold stock. You earn the difference between your price and the supplier's price, minus ads, platform and payment fees. The catch is that anyone can copy your product, ad costs decide your margin, and you carry the blame for slow shipping and poor quality you do not control.

body: A customer buys from your store at your price. You then place the order with your supplier at their price and give them the customer's address. Your profit per order is the gap, minus ad cost per sale, store subscription, payment fees, refunds and chargebacks.

Because there is no stock, the main cost is getting attention: paid ads on social media or search, or content and influencers. A product with a healthy markup can still lose money if each sale costs too much in ads.

ul: A store: a hosted e-commerce platform or a marketplace that allows dropshipping (check its policy).
A reliable supplier, ideally with stock in or near the country you sell to, tested with your own sample order.
A budget for ads and samples; the store itself is cheap, testing ads is not.
Clear shipping times, returns and contact details on your site.

Local paperwork: rules differ by country. Usually business registration and sales-tax or VAT handling. In the US, the FTC's mail-order rule requires you to ship within the time you state (or 30 days if you state none), or offer the buyer a delay or a refund.
Customer service time for tracking questions and complaints.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: People who like testing ads and reading numbers
Anyone who believes it is passive or easy
Someone with a small budget they can afford to lose on tests
People who cannot handle angry customers about delays
Marketers who can build a brand around a niche
Sellers wanting control over quality and packaging

ul: Courses and "winning product" lists: much of the dropshipping noise comes from people selling training, stores or product lists, not from selling products.
Shipping and quality: long delivery times and items that do not match the photos lead to refunds, chargebacks and payment processor holds.
Saturation: if a product is easy to find, many stores sell it and compete on ad price.
Legal and IP risk: unbranded copies of famous products, unsafe items or unsupported claims can bring takedowns or worse.
Payment holds: processors may hold funds for new stores with high dispute rates.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Pick a niche you understand and three products that solve a clear problem.
Order each one yourself to check delivery time, packaging and quality.
Calculate profit per order after supplier price, shipping, fees and a realistic ad cost.
Build a simple product page and spend a small, fixed ad budget you are willing to lose.
Stop or change the product if the cost per sale is above your margin.
Register the business and set up tax collection where required.
Choose one supplier and one niche, and write honest shipping and returns policies.
Launch with a few products, not hundreds.
Run small ad tests and track cost per sale, refunds and delivery times.
Answer every customer message quickly; reviews and disputes decide whether the store survives.

faq.a: The model is legal in most places, but you are still the seller: consumer protection, tax, product safety and advertising rules apply to you, and selling counterfeit or infringing goods is illegal.

faq.q: Do I need a business licence to dropship?
faq.a: It depends on where you live. Many places require business registration and sales-tax or VAT registration once you trade regularly. Check with your local tax authority.

faq.q: Is dropshipping better than holding stock?
faq.a: It lowers upfront cost but gives you less control and usually thinner margins. Many sellers start with dropshipping to test demand, then buy stock for products that prove themselves.
